utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm done with this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I asked you when we discussed your CV, Where were you serving late in 1993 and early 1994?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was chief of the security department of the 1st Army command in Belgrade at the time, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you take up that position, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you go back to the security administration?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got a transfer back to the security administration in early April 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were chief of security in the 1st Army, did you ever hear of the Drina plan?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were back to the security administration, did you perhaps then hear of the Drina plan?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please have P215. Thank you. You were shown this document during proofing, General. Did you ever see this document at any point in time before we commenced your proofing, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, Mr. Lukic. The first time I set eyes on this document was during proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw that document on the -- the remit of the security administration. We looked at all the organisational units of the General Staff of the VJ, and the security administration is involved in the drafting of a plan on the use of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm not saying you shouldn't show the witness the document, but he said he had never heard of the Drina plan, he'd never seen the Drina plan before until you proofed him. What can he tell us about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask the witness about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When plans such as this are produced, what is the role of the security organ in that process?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the security administration draws up what we call an attachment which is then attached to this kind of plan. It has two components. One is an assessment, and the other is a security plan, a single document with two components, hence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When a plan like this is drawn up at the strategic level, the level of the General Staff, are there any activities by the army at lower levels during the implementation? Particularly, I have in mind the security organ.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when a plan like this is drawn up at the strategic level, meaning the General Staff of the VJ, all the subordinate strategic commands, meaning the armies, must then be given other documents as well, a decision and an extract from a directive such as this, which then allows them to produce their own documents. The security organ at the level of an army would then use these excerpts from the security plan, which was produced by the General Staff, and then they would get this and produce the same kind of document at the army level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When a document like this is produced at the General Staff level, who proposes the part about the commitment of the security bodies, and who then goes on to approve it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security administration does, Mr. Lukic -- or, rather, an officer appointed by the chief of the security administration to be involved in the production of this plan, and the whole thing is approved by the person who normally approves all such documents, that being the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm done with this document. General, under the rules of service governing the work of security bodies, was any co-operation envisaged between the security organs and -- and the state security organs, and I mean the MUP bodies in charge of state security?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the former Yugoslavia, as we call it, there was a set of instructions called "Instructions regarding mutual relations and co-operation between the state security service and the security administration, the General Staff of the VJ." After Yugoslavia's break-up and once the new FRY was established, there was no new set of instructions. The old one applied. Nevertheless, it was never really used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In point of fact, throughout the period that we're talking about, and I'm sure you realise by now what we're looking into, specifically during the war between 1992 and 1995, what was your co-operation with the State Security Service of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To use a military term, tactical level and partially also at the operative level, it was fair and square. We dealt with some specific issues, specific cases involving foreign agencies, terrorism, crime, and so on and so forth. At the strategic level, the co-operation, however, was quite poor. I shall be bold enough to add that it wasn't our fault, but, rather, that of the other side, of our counterpart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say the strategic level, who exactly do you mean? And when you say your counterpart, who exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when I say the strategic level, I mean the security administration or the heads of the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was at the head of the state security of the Republic of Serbia at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the state security sector at the time was Mr. Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any sort of relationship in terms of communication and co-operation with the state security bodies of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, by way of a conclusion, I have only one topic left to raise before I can conclude my examination. During the war did you ever receive any information about crimes, specifically the crimes in Srebrenica and Sarajevo through any official intelligence reports?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic. That was never the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive anything from the security bodies in terms of reports talking about the crimes in Srebrenica and Sarajevo during the war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Lukic, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 01091D. This is a report of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, dated 21st of July, 1997, sent to the National Council for co-operation with the ICTY. You can see in the heading the basis for this request was the defence of Mr. Momcilo Perisic. Under 1, we can see that the military security and military intelligence agencies of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia are mentioned. Could you tell us, these bodies, which other bodies did they replace?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military security agency replaced the security administration of the -- of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia; and the military intelligence agency replaced the military intelligence administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please receive an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D275. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With this I have completed my examination, Mr. Gajic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. May I just have a moment to get myself organised?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General Gajic. My name is Dan Saxon, and I'm representing the Prosecution today.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have some questions for you, if I can. If I may, maybe I'll just start close to where Mr. Lukic left off. He showed you a plan that has been referred to as the Drina plan. It was Prosecution Exhibit P215. It's actually -- the full title is "The plan Drina for the use of the Yugoslav Army, Army of Republika Srpska, and the Serb Army of Krajina." And I believe you testified a few minutes ago that you had never heard of this plan, although you also explained the responsibilities of the security administration with respect to these kinds of plans, and you've testified today about the importance of the situation close to the border or the borders of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and how that was relevant and important to the security administration. And so I guess I would just ask you, first of all, in order to be able to protect the borders of the FRY during the armed conflict between 1993 and 1995, the -- the FRY, and, of course, the Army of Yugoslavia would want to have a plan in place, wouldn't it, in case, for example, an event such as Operation Storm or Operation Flash occurred?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you asked many different questions, so I will try to answer one by one. It is rather difficult to answer to this question which says "wouldn't it." But first of all, when it comes to the directive, I said that the first time I saw this directive was from the hands of Mr. Lukic. Before then I never saw it. Secondly, I said that while I was the chief of security department of the command of the 1st Army, I also never received any document that would have "Drina" in its title. When I came back to the security administration again, I never saw any document marked with the word "Drina." So the first time I saw a document marked with the word "Drina," this was when Counsel Lukic showed it to me. I never participated in its drafting, in any phase of its drafting. And secondly when you said that -- as I said, I never participated in drafting of the plans or this directive, and I talked about the obligations of the security organs when a similar war plan or directive was drafted. So whenever such a document was drafted at a security level, the security administration would always provide its contribution, and that contribution would consist of two elements, the textual element and a table that would be called a plan of security. So I can't really answer any questions concerning this particular document because I never saw it. I did not participate in --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, sorry. I never suggested that you had seen this document, and I haven't asked you about this document. Let me try to ask my question more simply. Given the circumstances taking place in the area of the former Yugoslavia in 1994/1995, as a prudent armed force, the Army of Yugoslavia needed to have a plan in case the security of its borders were threatened; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It had its war plan. The Army of Yugoslavia did have the war plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And this plan, in case -- for example, in case Croatian forces threatened to invade the -- or did invade the territories of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and Republika Srpska, what was the -- what was the plan to defend the borders of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in case of an aggression, we had a defence plan for the protection of the territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the name of that plan?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I can say this. I'm not sure that I'm not under the obligation to protect this confidential information concerning the name of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I'll withdraw my question. Can you tell us where such a plan has been recorded or kept?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would suggest if we continue with this line of questioning to move into a private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Gajic, on Wednesday at -- this is at page 10840 of the transcript. You agreed with the proposition put to you by Mr. Lukic that the VJ, the VRS, and the SVK were "three entirely separate and independent armies." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And again yesterday, this is at pages 10842 to 10843, you described how the chief of the intelligence security sector of the VRS was Colonel and later General Zdravko Tolimir. You described how Ljubisa Beara was chief of the VRS military security sector, and how Colonel Petar Salapura was the chief of military intelligence for the VRS. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you aware that each of these men were assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre of the Army of Yugoslavia? I should say, of the General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that they were on the register of the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can we show the witness what is P2698, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Gajic, this is an extract of the VJ personnel file of Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down a bit, please, in the B/C/S version. And if we could go to page 5 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, if you direct your attention to the second row from the bottom, you'll see it says there that Petar Salapura was transferred and assigned to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia's 30th Personnel Centre. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please read this once again? I have difficulty reading this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please scroll to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see in the left-hand corner it says -- left-hand column, it says: "Transferred and assigned in keeping with MF outside the garrison due to service requirements, chief of intelligence department." And the next column to the right: "General Staff, 30th Personnel Centre, Belgrade garrison." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then further to the right, we see, "10 November 1993." So can we agree that Colonel Salapura was transferred and assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, he was merely registered in the 30th personnel centre in order to be able to resolve his status-related and social entitlements, and this was the purpose for which the 30th Personnel Centre was established, the 30th Personnel Centre which was, as far as I know, under the administration for personnel affairs of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Saxon, I'm sorry to interrupt you. You've referred to this column which says, "10th November 1993." What is the heading of that column at the beginning of this chapter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Period from-to."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, sir, can we agree on this: The document says, "transferred and assigned," does it not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what the document says, but I explained what was the function of the 30th Personnel Centre and why it was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And military documents are meant to be precise; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am not an expert for personnel issues. I am a counter-intelligence officer, and I can tell you as much as I know concerning the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you now. I asked you a very simple question. I'll repeat it, and I'd like an answer. Military documents are meant to be precise; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show -- we can leave this document, and can we show P2128, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see here the first page. We see in handwriting, "Order by the chief, PRU, number 5-34." And then we see, "9, 7 February 1994." General Gajic, are you aware whether the acronym PRU refers to personnel, or personnel order or administration?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't say that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what PRU stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we move to the next page in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could focus on what's at the top of the screen, please. Are you following me, General?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 3 in the English version, please, and the next page in the B/C/S version. And if you -- actually, Mr. Registrar, if you could focus on number 3, which is starting in the middle of the page in the B/C/S version to make it easier for General Gajic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, General Gajic, if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again we see an order related to Petar Salapura. It says: "At the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia." And, actually -- "30th Personnel Centre, Main Staff, as chief of the intelligence department."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we go to the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see what it says. "He is transferred and appointed as per the needs of the service, effective 10 November 1993, when the establishment was prescribed." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is this? We are talking about Petar Salapura, are we? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the bottom of the page in your version.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then if you look -- can we go one page forward in the B/C/S version. Same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there we see "Zdravko Tolimir."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see Mr. Lukic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on the previous page you can see the name and the surname in B/C/S, so possibly the witness should be shown the previous page, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Could we move back to the previous page and focus on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see Mr. Tolimir is mentioned there? Item number 4.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we then go to the next page in Serbo-Croat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see now that Mr. Tolimir is at the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, he's being transferred and appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre, Main Staff, as assistant chief. Again, below, he is transferred and appointed as per the needs of the service, effective 10 November 1993. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I see the time. Shall we pause now and we'll continue with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Gajic, we were reviewing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Saxon, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We were reviewing what is Exhibit P2128, and I believe when we stopped we were looking at the entry for Colonel Tolimir. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where he is transferred and appointed as per the needs of the service, effective 10 November 1993. And he's being transferred and appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre. Isn't that what this document indicates?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please turn to page 17 in the English version. And I will give a page number in the Serbo-Croat version, if I can. And if we could -- actually, can we please go forward one page in B/C/S, please. And if we could - thank you - zoom in on what is number 27. And if we could scroll to the bottom of the page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you'll see here, General Gajic, Ljubisa Beara, a gentleman who you knew, to the Yugoslav army General Staff, 30th Personnel Centre, as chief of department. And on the right-hand side we see the date, 10 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move forward one page in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, again with respect to Mr. Beara, that he was also -- he was transferred and appointed as per the needs of the service. Do you see that, General Gajic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So can we agree that Ljubisa Beara was also transferred and appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, his record was being kept by the 30th Personnel Centre so that he could avail himself of his social benefits and status entitlements. As far as I know as I said yesterday he was the chief of the security administration and the General Staff of the VJ. Therefore, he was outside the chain of command of the VJ and was now part of the chain of command of the VRS. I have to say I am no professional in this matter, but that is my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, do I take your response, General, to my question as a yes or as a no?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll repeat it. I thought it was pretty clear. My question was, can we agree that Ljubisa Beara was also transferred and appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre? You can answer "Yes," "No," "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I explained what I believe the answer should be. I know of no other answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can we agree that the document, this order that was issued in February 1994, uses the language "transferred and appointed," doesn't it? Isn't that the language that we saw?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The document doesn't use the term, "is registered in the 30th Personnel Centre," does it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Svetozar Kosoric from the JNA and the Army of Yugoslavia? I'll spell that, K-o-s-o-r-i-c, with the diacritic. Svetozar Kosoric. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That name doesn't ring a bell, not based on what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit P2518, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I believe it's confidential, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. You're absolutely correct. Can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. 12 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic -- I beg your pardon. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll take that as a compliment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at this document, General Gajic, you will see it is a request from the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army, dated the 23rd of May, 1995, titled, "Request, sending officers on assignment pursuant to Article 58 of the Yugoslav Army Law." And then we see it says stamped "personally to," and then "the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this document is from the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the VRS, lieutenant General Manojlo Jovanovic. And it says: "Based on the real need for the engagement of specific Yugoslav Army officers in VRS commands and units, we request you to send the following officers for temporary assistance, pursuant to Article 58 of the Yugoslav Army Law." And the first officer, forgive me if I'm mispronouncing his name, Svetozar Kosoric, son of Djoko, lieutenant-colonel. "Currently chief of the VJ special units corps armoured brigade, organ for intelligence affairs, in order to appoint him as the chief of the VRS Drina Corps Command Department for Intelligences Affairs." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see the second gentleman, Branko Karlica. "Currently a desk officer at the Yugoslav Army General Staff 2nd administration." Did you know Branko Karlica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officer number one and officer number two are members of the military intelligence administration not of the security administration of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Fine. My question was, Did you know Branko Karlica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "... the mentioned officers have expressed their willingness to be temporarily assigned and sent to the relevant VRS commands, whereby their status should be regulated adequately with their appointments in the VJ units being put on temporary stay." And then it says: "As the mentioned officers have a professional background that is crucial to us, and as they were born in these territories, we hope that you will have understanding." Have you been following me?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness -- and, Your Honours, we can move back into public session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will do that -- I just wanted to check something. You ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I assist you, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No thanks. You did not need to assist me. The transcript has done so. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show General Gajic Exhibit P2103.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And here we see a document, General Gajic, from the Drina Corps commander, dated the 20th of August, 1995, by which Svetozar Kosoric has been appointed as the chief of the intelligence department, the intelligence security organ and the ground forces of the corps, the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff, the army of Yugoslav Army. You see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll to the -- can we go to the -- can we go to the next page in English. Excuse me. If we stay on the -- I'm sorry. Can we please go back to the first page in English. It's my fault. Focus on the bottom of the page, please. And can we please scroll down in the B/C/S version. So we see the document explains that Mr. Kosoric has been standing in as -- for the chief of the intelligence department in accordance with this order from the 19th of June, 1995. Can we go to the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the last section or provision, we see the words "Statement of reasons." And it says: "Chief of intelligence department formation post at ground forces corps, the 30th Personnel Centre, General Staff of the VJ, has been unfulfilled for a longer period of time, so Acting Officer had to be appointed until replenishment will be perform in any other way." So we see that Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric -- excuse me, Colonel Kosoric was appointed in this position through the 30th Personnel Centre; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've explained that, and I have nothing to add. I said as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know Vujadin Popovic, sir, in the JNA, in the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You didn't know them, or you don't remember? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness P2066, please. And that does not look like the right exhibit at all. Is that P2066? 2066. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Gajic, this is an extract, if you will, from the VJ personnel file of Vujadin Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could turn, please, to page 2 in the English version, please. And if we could focus -- there we go. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you'll see, General Gajic, around halfway down the page in your version we see that Mr. Popovic became the head of the security department in the intelligence security organ in the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff of the VJ beginning on the 1st of February, 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can remain in private session. Did you know a gentleman, sir, named Radoslav Jankovic in the JNA, the VJ?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: You'll see, General Gajic, this is a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, dated the 25th of April, 1995. There's a handwritten note at the top. utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And his position was what?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, he was chief of the military intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the document says: "Please, as soon as possible send us the following officers for duty in the VRS Main Staff intelligence administration." "On your request he was temporarily reassigned to the VRS Main Staff intelligence administration where he spent two months. "Both persons are born in the territory of the Republika Srpska, where their parents still reside." And then it says: "As the VRS Main Staff administration remains undermanned, there are only four officers and one non-commissioned officer, but the extent of the job is increasing, especially in the section for analysis. I kindly ask you to grant this request as soon as possible." And then we see that it's from General Ratko Mladic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then there is message at the bottom of the page from Sinisa Borovic, addressed to, "Sir, Colonel." "We forward you the VRS Main Staff telegram and inform you that the chief of the VJ General Staff ordered: 'Krga, proposal, but after talks with them.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please move back into public session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: With the document still on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Without it, Your Honour. We can leave this document now. Thank you.

utterances.text: Main the document please be removed, and may the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.text: And I'd like to play some excerpts from what is P438, some video material.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Gajic, I'm going to show you some video material from a meeting that was held at the Hotel Fontana in the town of Bratunac, in Republika Srpska, on the 13th of July, 1995. utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, the man facing us -- we're at 1:42:52. General, the man facing us who is bald with the moustache has been identified in testimony before this Chamber as Colonel Svetozar Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue now to 1:44:30, and then start again, please. Just fast-forward, please. Can we move forward, please. It's very difficult to see. Can we move forward, please, to 1:45:09.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we stop there at 1:45:11, again at the far right-hand corner of the table we see Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we fast forward, please, to 1:50:29.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, the man facing us on the other side of the table, this is at 1:50:29, with the moustache, has been identified by witnesses in these proceedings as Colonel Vujadin Popovic. And if we could -- and the man at the end of the table, on the left end, facing us, has been identified as Radoslav Jankovic. Now, my question for you is, you've talked about the fact that you knew Mr. Tolimir, Salapura, Beara, because you knew them from the security intelligence organs, that they were serving in the VRS. We've just seen these gentlemen here, Kosoric, Popovic, Jankovic, also serving in the VRS, coming from the Army of Yugoslavia. I want to go back to your position that you made earlier about these being separate and independent armies. Wouldn't it be fair to say, General Gajic, that the VRS was dependent on the VJ for its senior-level security and intelligence officers? Isn't that really what this evidence shows?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. We can't --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can also explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You started, if you excuse me, by asking me the questions that should have come later, and you didn't ask me what I tried to explain, and this is how the 30th Personnel Centre was set up and what its role actually was. So these were officers who were -- who were dispatched and voluntarily so. You saw from the documents that interviews were carried out with them. So they were dispatched voluntarily to the Army of Republika Srpska, and they were appointed at certain positions within the Army of Republika Srpska. So they were outside the chain of command of the VJ, and they were now within the chain of command of the Army of Republika Srpska. The 30th Personnel Centre was formed, if you allow me -- please allow me, because these are some of the principal issues. The 30th Personnel Centre was formed in order to keep the records of these persons so that these persons could regulate their status-related issues which they were entitled to pursuant to law. This is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Gajic, where did you see in the documents that I've shown you that these gentlemen were dispatched voluntarily to the Army of Republika Srpska? Where did you see that? Where did I show you a document that Ljubisa Beara was dispatched voluntarily to the Army of Republika Srpska, Petar Salapura --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon now asked three questions. First of all, a general question and then some specific questions. So possibly he would like to rephrase those questions, or ask them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My colleague makes a fair point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If -- I may not remember which of these exhibits you showed us, but there's one where it was talking about two gentlemen who were interviewed and said they were willing to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go back to that. Ah, yes. Can we -- can we show the witness what is P2518, please. And can the Registry help me whether this is a -- can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. Sorry, Mr. Court Usher. 8 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we scroll down to the bottom of the page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see in this document, General Gajic, that you are right with respect to these two individuals, Svetozar Kosoric and Branko Karlica. It says that they have expressed their willingness to be temporarily assigned and sent to the relevant VRS commands. Now, can we move out of public session? We don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into -- do you want to stay in closed session while you object, sir, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing I would like to say. Possibly we can clarify this with the witness now or I'll do it in my redirect, but we have a significant problem with the translation of the portion that was in the original written by hand. We have a problem with the translation of that part. But I apologise, Your Honours. I will address this issue in my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May the document please be removed from the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document please be removed from the screen. Thank you. It has now been removed. May the Chamber now move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't think you've really answered -- you've really explained your response, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the question that you had asked was: "Where in any of the documents that I've shown you is it mentioned that they went willingly." Now, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we've seen -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now the exhibit has answered you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, so he has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He has, Your Honour. I'm going to move back to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I had asked you, General Gajic, wouldn't it be fair to say that the VRS was dependent on the Army of Yugoslavia for its senior-level security and intelligence officers, and you said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So he answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That is correct. I will move on now to a different topic. Can we show the witness, please, what is P1151. We can stay in public session. Actually, it's a related topic. It's still related to this issue of separate and independent armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see, General, that this is a document from the Main Staff, the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, personnel administration, the 40th Personnel Centre. It's addressed to the Main Staff of the 40th Personnel Centre. And we see here it says that: "The Army of Yugoslavia Military School -- Military Centre, requests that Djuro Vojkovic, Captain 1st Class, return to the duty in the military school centre of the VJ as soon as possible due to special needs of the service." And then it explains: "He is currently in the 11th Corps of the 40th Personnel Centre, where he was sent temporarily pursuant to Article 271 of the Law on the Service in the Armed Forces." And it requests that Captain Vojkovic be issued with the authorisation to return to his parent unit. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So after the Army of Yugoslavia transferred officers to the Army of Serbian Krajina via the 40th Personnel Centre, they would also arrange sometimes to bring them home if the needs of the Army of Yugoslavia required it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the way this question was posed is a rather complicated one. [In English] If the Army of Yugoslavia transferred officers to the Army of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I can break it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After VJ officers were assigned to the 40th Personnel Centre and served in the army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, the VJ also, if their needs -- the VJ also would call them back if their needs depended on it; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this would be my interpretation of this document. The Captain 1st Class of the Technical Service, Vojnovic [sic], Djuro, during an interview agreed voluntarily to join the Army of Serbian Krajina. At that point he exited from the chain of command of the VJ and entered the chain of command of the Army of Serbian Krajina where he was appointed at a particular duty. And in order for his status to be regulated, his record was entered into the records of the 40th Personnel Centre. Then it was estimated the Army of Yugoslavia for this person who voluntarily left, that he was needed because of the combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia, and for that reason it was requested that he returned because he was needed for the combat readiness which was always our primary task. So this is my interpretation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, all right. Let me -- let's talk about your response, please, step-by-step. You say that this document indicates that Captain 1st Class Vojnovic [sic], during an interview agreed voluntarily to join the Army of Serbian Krajina. Can you tell us where within the four corners of this document we see that information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we cannot see that first part. That is what we are lacking here. We do not have any explanation of the conditions within which this person left. So it was decision of the Supreme Defence Council, and they were orders of the president of the FRY and Chief of the General Staff to form the personnel centres, and pursuant to all these decisions the officers could be sent to the Army of Republika Srpska and Serbian Krajina only voluntarily, only following an interview, and only if they signed a statement to the effect that they went there voluntarily. This is what we can't see here, but I know that these orders were in place, that these decisions were in place, and this is why I conclude that the same procedure was undertaken for Mr. Vojnovic [sic], and I can only assume that he was also born in the territory of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Let's take this a little bit more slowly, please. If I understand your response, not just to my last question but to the question before that, you said that it was requested that Captain Vojnovic [sic] be returned because he was needed for the combat readiness, "which was always our primary task." So the point being Captain Vojnovic [sic] was needed for the readiness of the VJ. Is that what was happening here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it is said here that he had to report to the duty at the centre of military schools of the Army of Yugoslavia. So this was the educational institution, and he was probably needed there. I do not know what his speciality was. I can't read that anywhere in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness P2598, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We're going to -- we're not going to focus on Captain Vojnovic [sic] any more. You'll see, General Gajic, this is an order of the chief of the personnel administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, dated 17 June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll up in the English, please. Scroll up in the English, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see at the top, it says: "Order number 5-193." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And the first page tells us that: "Pursuant to item 7, subparagraph 4 and 5," et cetera, "... on determining authorities and on responsibilities of commanding officers in solving relations in the service of the Army of Yugoslavia ..." We see a number of people is appointed as per peacetime establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please go to page 9 in the English version and page 8 in the B/C/S version. And if we could actually focus on the bottom of the page, please. Bottom of the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you take a look, General, at item 13. Above that we see the heading, "To 1st Army ... operations group 'Drina.'" And below that, number 13, we see: "Tihomir Babic, son of Zivko, Infantry Captain 1st Class ... to the Loznica Garrison." Dated 17 June, 1994. And then it says: "Now: Duty post at the 30th Personnel Centre of the Yugoslav Army General Staff ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in English, please. And if we could focus on the top of the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, we're looking at a line that begins with, "Responsible commanding officer." Do you have that in your page in the bottom? It says --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "Responsible commanding officer will appoint the named person immediately. Upon receipt of the document on appointment, he shall be immediately released from duty as per peacetime and sent to the new duty."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, can we please leave this document, and can we show the witness Exhibit P1856.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I needed to show him this document as an introduction to the document that's coming, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Gajic, this document is from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska, Sector for Organisation, Mobilisation and Personnel. It's dated 14th of August, 1994. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "Tihomir Babic, Captain 1st Class." Then it says: "Execution of an order regarding transfer. To the command of the Drina Corps." It says: "Further to an order number 5-193, dated 17 June 1994," which was the order that we just saw, P1151 -- excuse me, P2598. It says further to that order: "Tihomir Babic, Infantry Captain 1st Class, is transferred from the 30th Personnel Centre to the VJ unit." And then it says: "The aforementioned shall be forthwith discharged from his present unit and dispatched into transfer." Have you been following me?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, this document that we're looking at now, this execution of an order regarding transfer, it's issued by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what is written at the top of the document, "Main Staff, Army of the Republika Srpska, Sector for Organisation, Mobilisation, Personnel."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Please help us with this: If the VJ and the VRS were two separate and independent armies, how is it that an officer in the VRS Main Staff had the power to execute an order to transfer Captain Babic from a VJ General Staff unit to another VJ army unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objections regarding this question, but I would kindly ask the interpreters to repeat their interpretation into Serbian of the question by Mr. Saxon. The way it has been interpreted, I believe it might cause some confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Interpreters, will you please repeat the interpretation to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we have exactly the reverse here of what we had previously. We have Babic Tihomir, son of Zivko, an officer, who was sent on a voluntary basis to the VRS, meaning he was now outside the chain of command of the VJ. He was appointed not to the Main Staff of the VRS but, rather, to the Hercegovina Corps. On the left-hand side, towards the bottom of the document, you will find the signature of Assistant Commander Major General Mico Grubor. It is very likely, although we have no -- none of the previous documents which I suppose should exist, that the army had the need for Babic Tihomir, son of Zivko, to be returned to the VJ and appointed to the Loznica unit with the VJ. Most probably there had been a request by the VJ for that officer to be relieved of his duties with the VRS. He was now outside the chain of command of the VRS. And then through the 30th Personnel Centre, he was taken off the file in terms of social benefits and his status there and was now back within the chain of command of the VJ. An order is here issued for his appointment to the VJ. That is my understanding, and I believe my interpretation is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The thing is, General, that you haven't answered my question. We've reviewed the documents. We know what the documents say. But my question -- I didn't ask you to tell us what the documents say. Let me lay out the situation here for you. We saw Exhibit P2598 which was the document bearing order number 5-193. That contained the order for Captain Tihomir Babic to be transferred from the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff of the VJ to a position in the 1st Army. And now on our screen we see P1856, which is a document issued by a member of the VRS entitled, "Execution of an order regarding transfer," regarding Captain Babic. And I'll repeat my question. You told us very emphatically yesterday that the VRS -- well, that the VRS, the SVK, and the VJ were three separate and independent armies. So my question is: If the VJ and the VRS were two separate and independent armies, how is it that an officer in the VRS had the power to execute an order to transfer Captain Babic from a unit of the VJ General Staff to another unit of the VJ? Help us understand this, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I answered this question to the best of my ability. I am not a personnel officer. I'm no professional in that field. I stand by my previous answers, which doesn't mean you may not come across better qualified individuals to study this particular issue. I know what I know, and I have said as much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, the difficulty I have with that response, General Gajic, is that you've made some very emphatic propositions about personnel-related matters today in response to my question about what it -- what the 30th Personnel Centre was, about how persons came to become members of the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina. So it's difficult for me, then, to understand your last response, which now you're saying you don't know too much about personnel-related matters.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm afraid you didn't understand. I answered based on the decisions and orders regulating the issue in the spirit of the law. If I have failed to meet your expectations, I can only say that I'm sorry, but I am unable to offer any other answer. I stand by my answer. My answer is based on decisions and orders. I did not deal with these issues. You're asking me about personnel-related matters here. You have shown me some of these forms and documents, that there were things there that I simply don't understand. I am not privy to the technicalities, and they're very hard for me to decipher. You asked me to explain; I have to say I did my best to help you along with this, but I can't be expected to say something I simply don't know. It wouldn't be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I certainly accept that, General. Would it be fair then to say that you weren't privy to all the technicalities regarding whether these were three separate and independent armies or not? Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, whether these were, in fact, three independent and separate armies, I have to be categorical about that. They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you weren't privy to all of the technicalities that might have -- that might shed some light on this particular topic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Saxon is very close to speculation or asking the witness to speculate with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm asking a factual question. I'm testing the evidence of this witness. I'm following up one of his questions with a question of my own. I don't think that there's anything speculative about my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you want me to repeat my question, General Gajic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're categorical about the in fact these were three independent and separate armies, and my question for you is: You weren't privy to all of the technicalities - that was the term you used - that might shed some light on this particular topic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I explained everything I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move to another topic. I see it's 5 to 7.00. Can we pause at this time, or do you want me to start another topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are in your hands, Mr. Saxon. If you want us to pause, we shall pause. I don't know how long the next topic is going to take. You know better.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It will take a while, Your Honour, so if we could pause, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a technical issue to raise before we break for the day. We sit in the morning tomorrow. Could I please be given an indication on the length of the remaining cross by Mr. Saxon? I have an idea about my own re-examination. I am asking this in view of the next witness who is lined up, if there is too little time left for the next witness, and I am also in charge of examining the next witness. I'm not sure about Mr. Saxon's position regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, are you able to help your colleague?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I can say I believe I will take at least one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does that help you, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have at least a session for my re-examination. Therefore, if there is still some daylight after that, as they say, I will try to see what the Chamber's position is in terms of maybe not calling the next witness if there's too little time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the Chamber hear you at the time, sir? Let's cross the bridge when we get to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Your Honour. I was just wondering whether I should bring the witness into the building and keep him waiting here, but we can, as you said, cross that bridge when we come to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: From what both of you have said, it looks like we will use two sessions tomorrow. Mr. Saxon will take at least a session. You will take perhaps another session to re-examine. I don't know whether there are questions from the Bench which might take whatever time they take, and then questions by the parties after the questions by the Bench. So it's very difficult for me to come to your rescue, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll see how things pan out. We'll be ready if you give us the go-ahead, but we'll wait up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Sir, unfortunately, we are not done with you. You will still have to come back tomorrow, but tomorrow we start early in the morning, not in the afternoon. We start at 9.00 in Courtroom III. Once again I remind you that you may not discuss the case with anybody, and in particular not with your -- the counsel for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. The matter stands adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00 in Courtroom III. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
